office_does: A Stevens PUD commissioner sits on the three-member board of an elected water and sewer utility serving about 5,000 customers in Stevens County and parts of Spokane County, for a six-year term.
race_blurb: Every voter in the PUD, including its small Spokane County portion, votes on the District 2 seat. Commissioner Howie Kubik, a retired Avista lineman who has held the seat for 17 years without recent opposition, faces registered nurse Andrea Morgan, who stresses preventive maintenance, predictable rates and transparency.

candidates.summary: Incumbent PUD commissioner for 17 years (self-reported) and a retired 37-year Avista lineman and foreman, running on reliable, safe and cost-effective water and sewer service.
highlights: PUD commissioner for 17 years; re-elected unopposed in 2014 and 2020 [S1][S2][S3]
Retired after 37 years at Avista as a lineman, foreman and local representative [S1]
Says he has worked for reliable, safe and cost-effective utility service [S1]

candidates.summary: Registered nurse of nearly 40 years and 33-year Stevens County property owner running for her first office, stressing preventive maintenance, predictable rates and transparency.
highlights: Registered nurse for nearly 40 years; no prior elected office [S1]
Prioritizes preventive maintenance and long-term stability to keep rates predictable [S1]
Wants to balance infrastructure needs with natural resources and private property rights [S1]
